territorial_scope.description: Applies to covered U.S. persons, including U.S.-organized entities' foreign branches and persons located in the United States, so it reaches U.S.-linked actors outside U.S. territory.

summary.short: Proposed BIS rule adding 15 CFR 702.7 to require covered U.S. persons to notify the Department quarterly of planned AI model training runs above 10^26 operations or qualifying computing clusters, and to answer BIS questions on model security and safety.
summary.long: The proposed rule amends 15 CFR part 702 by adding section 702.7 on on-going reporting for advanced AI development. Covered U.S. persons, defined to include U.S. citizens, lawful permanent residents, entities organized under U.S. law (including foreign branches), and persons located in the United States, must email BIS each quarter (April 15, July 15, October 15, January 15) if they conduct or plan within six months an AI training run above 10^26 computational operations, or acquire or develop a computing cluster with data center networking above 300 Gbit/s and a theoretical maximum above 10^20 OP/s for AI training without sparsity. Each notification identifies planned activities for the following six months. Covered persons must answer BIS questions within 30 calendar days, correct incomplete filings within 14 calendar days of BIS notice, answer clarification questions within seven calendar days, and submit quarterly affirmations of no applicable activities for up to seven quarters. BIS questions may address training, ownership and protection of model weights, red-team results, and safety and reliability of dual-use foundation models. Section 702.7(c) defines terms including AI model, AI system, AI red-teaming, dual-use foundation model, model weights and training run. The text states no effective date and no penalties.

notes: Proposed rule text (NPRM), not a final rule; the document gives no effective date, and the preamble is not included. The authority citation adds E.O. 14110, and the text does not state whether that order remains in force. The defined term 'Large-scale computing cluster' refers to the thresholds in paragraph (a)(1), but operative paragraph (a)(1)(ii) uses 'computing cluster'; the defined term is not used in the operative text. Target_instrument_id is empty for targets not in the registry.
